newsitem.title: USA: Sales of single-family homes reach record levels.
newsitem.headline: Sales of single-family homes reach record levels.

text.p: Rhode Island Association of Realtors said sales of existing family homes reached record levels during the first nine months of 1996, Providence Journal reported Wednesday.
The 5,115 houses sold from January to September represented an 11 percent hike over the same period a year earlier. The previous record was 5,081 set in 1994, the newspaper reported.
The median sales price in the state was $117,000 during the third quarter, up $4,500 from the median price in the first quarter of 1996, the newspaper said. Average time on the market was 138 days.
Sales figures were based on the association's statewide multiple listing service through which 65 percent of all house sales are handled, the newspaper said.
But the existng home sales figures could be misleading one economist told the newspaper.

"Existing home sales have done very well, but new construction is awful, absolutely horrible," University of Rhode Island economist Leonard Lardaro told the Journal. "We're barely above the 2,000 level (single family building permits) at an annual rate.
"Anyone who judges the entire housing sector by existing home sales will come to seriously wrong conclusions...New home construction has not been part of this recovery," he said.
